newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended mixed with golds rising on a better bullion price and industrials steady amid profit-taking.
Dealers said gold, which rose above the $320 level overnight amid shortcovering, was the main driver behind sentiment.
The metal was fixed at $324.20 on Friday afternoon in London, up from the morning fix of $323.45.
Among the sector's best performers on the day were Freegold, which added 90 cents to 23.50 rand and Western Deep, which rose 400 cents to 108 rand. Vaal Reefs climbed 12.50 rand to 234.50 rand.
Overall volumes traded were hefty again with turnover of 1.13 billion rand boosted by engineering holding firm Invicta which hovered at 580 cents after shares worth 58 million rand changed hands.
Uniserv, which does business as Sun Couriers, saw large turnover of 18.0 million rand on the back of overnight foreign buying. It was last down 115 cents to 825 cents.
Gold shares rose 27.7 points to 992 points, the all-share index lost 12.1 points to 7,424.9 points and industrials were down 3.5 points to 8,937.7 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues outpaced decliners by 202 to 190 with 137 issues unchanged.
There were 33 shares which surged to new highs while 20 sank to new lows.
The market was seen taking a cue from a variety of sources next week although much of the market's attention would remain focused on gold, dealers and portfolio managers said on Friday.

"It will depend on how the gold price behaves. If the weaker rand, gold price and bonds continue...the market will probably go weak," Johan Marais, director at stockbroking firm Societe General Frankel Pollack, told Reuters.
Near-dated all-share and industrial share futures tumbled after S&P futures fell through the initial 15 point limit at start of trade.
Dealers said gold contracts were last firm on a firmer bullion price. The futures market was seen looking to the gold price and Wall Street for direction next week.
The September all-share contract was last at 6,675/98 from 6,755, industrial contract at 8,500/10 from 8,573 and gold contract at 700/20 from 691.
